microtheory.name: psychoacoustics
microtheory.definition: How humans perceive sound. Masking, critical bands, pitch perception, loudness scaling, sound localization, timbre perception. The bridge between acoustics + auditory cortex. Substrate analogue: directly describes what the substrate's cochlear pipeline + auditory_cortex compute.

concepts.name: critical_band
concepts.definition: Fletcher 1940. Bandwidth around a tone within which other tones interact (mask, beat). ~100 Hz wide at low frequencies, ~20% of center frequency at high. Maps onto basilar membrane regions. Substrate analogue: substrate's gammatone bandwidth — designed to match critical bands.

concepts.name: bark_scale
concepts.definition: Zwicker 1961. Perceptual frequency scale: 1 Bark = 1 critical band. ~24 Barks span audible range. Substrate analogue: substrate's gammatone channel spacing.

concepts.name: erb_scale
concepts.definition: Moore + Glasberg 1983. Equivalent Rectangular Bandwidth — refined Bark. ERB(f) = 24.7(0.00437f + 1). Substrate analogue: substrate's gammatone bandwidth formula.

concepts.name: mel_scale
concepts.definition: Stevens 1937. Perceptual pitch scale. 1000 mel = 1000 Hz; doubles for pitch perceived as doubled. Linear below 500 Hz, log above. Substrate analogue: substrate's pitch normalization.

concepts.name: absolute_threshold
concepts.definition: Minimum SPL at which a tone is detectable. Most sensitive ~2-4 kHz. Substrate analogue: substrate's per-channel input gating threshold.

concepts.name: equal_loudness_contour
concepts.definition: Fletcher + Munson 1933, refined ISO 226. Curves of equal-perceived-loudness across frequency at different intensities. Low + high frequencies need more SPL for same loudness. Substrate analogue: substrate's frequency-weighted loudness integration.

concepts.name: phon
concepts.definition: Loudness level — SPL of equally-loud 1kHz tone. 1kHz tone @ 40dB SPL = 40 phon. Substrate analogue: substrate's normalized loudness output.

concepts.name: sone
concepts.definition: Subjective loudness. 1 sone = 40 phon = 1 kHz @ 40 dB SPL. Doubles per 10 phon. Stevens' power law. Substrate analogue: substrate's perceptual-loudness output.

concepts.name: simultaneous_masking
concepts.definition: Tone masked by simultaneous noise/tone in same critical band. Spectral masking. Substrate analogue: substrate's within-channel competition.

concepts.name: temporal_masking
concepts.definition: Forward masking (after sound) + backward masking (before sound). Within ~200ms. Substrate analogue: substrate's channel temporal recovery.

concepts.name: comodulation_masking_release
concepts.definition: Hall 1984. Adding off-frequency noise can REDUCE masking when modulation pattern is shared. Substrate analogue: substrate's cross-channel grouping by common envelope.

concepts.name: pitch_perception_models
concepts.definition: Two main: place theory (basilar membrane location, Helmholtz) vs temporal theory (firing periodicity, Wever). Modern view: complementary. Substrate analogue: substrate's pitch detector combines place + periodicity.

concepts.name: missing_fundamental
concepts.definition: Perceive pitch of F0 even when F0 is filtered out — brain reconstructs from harmonics. Schouten 1940. Refutes pure-place theory. Substrate analogue: substrate's harmonic-template-driven pitch.

concepts.name: virtual_pitch
concepts.definition: Pitch perceived at F0 from harmonic stack. Terhardt's template theory. Substrate analogue: substrate's harmonic-pattern matching.

concepts.name: pitch_chroma
concepts.definition: Two octave-related notes share chroma + height. Helix model of pitch (Shepard). Substrate analogue: substrate's octave-modular pitch representation.

concepts.name: shepard_tone
concepts.definition: Octave-spaced sinusoids with envelope. Produces endless ascending illusion. Substrate analogue: substrate's pitch-helix decoupling demo.

concepts.name: interaural_time_difference
concepts.definition: ITD. Sound from right reaches right ear ~0.7ms before left. Used for localization below ~1.5 kHz. Substrate analogue: substrate's bilateral arrival-time comparator.

concepts.name: interaural_level_difference
concepts.definition: ILD. Head shadow makes ipsilateral ear louder. Used above ~1.5 kHz where wavelength < head. Substrate analogue: substrate's bilateral amplitude comparator.

concepts.name: head_related_transfer_function
concepts.definition: HRTF. Spectral filtering by pinna + head + torso. Encodes elevation + front-back. Highly individualized. Substrate analogue: substrate's per-source spectral signature.

concepts.name: precedence_effect
concepts.definition: Wallach + Newman + Rosenzweig 1949. Source perceived at the direction of FIRST arrival; later reflections suppress spatial info. Substrate analogue: substrate's first-arrival prioritization.

concepts.name: auditory_scene_analysis
concepts.definition: Bregman 1990. Cortex parses overlapping sounds into separate streams. Simultaneous (vertical) + sequential (horizontal) grouping. Substrate analogue: substrate's source-stream separation.

concepts.name: stream_segregation
concepts.definition: Sequential sounds form streams based on pitch proximity, timbre, location. Substrate analogue: substrate's temporal stream grouping.

concepts.name: cocktail_party_problem
concepts.definition: Cherry 1953. Separating one conversation from many. Computational neuroscience challenge. Substrate analogue: substrate's source-isolation problem.

concepts.name: schema_based_grouping
concepts.definition: Top-down familiar pattern recognition aids source separation. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt-driven expectations biasing scene analysis.

rules.name: critical_bands_define_perceptual_resolution
rules.head: the substrate processes spectral information
rules.body: frequency resolution is limited by critical band width — within a critical band, components interact + mask. Substrate's gammatone bandwidth implements this.

rules.name: equal_loudness_compensation_required
rules.head: the substrate computes perceived loudness from spectrum
rules.body: low + high frequencies need higher SPL for same perceived loudness. Fletcher + Munson. Substrate's loudness integration must frequency-weight.

rules.name: pitch_combines_place_and_periodicity
rules.head: the substrate detects pitch of a complex tone
rules.body: it uses both spectral peak locations (place) and temporal firing patterns (periodicity). Missing fundamental shows neither alone is sufficient.

rules.name: itd_and_ild_complement_for_localization
rules.head: the substrate localizes a sound source
rules.body: ITD dominates below ~1.5kHz; ILD dominates above. Both required for full azimuth resolution. Substrate's bilateral processing.

rules.name: precedence_effect_suppresses_echo_localization
rules.head: the substrate receives a direct sound followed by reflections within 30ms
rules.body: it localizes to the first arrival; the reflections color but don't separately localize. Substrate's echo-robust localization.

rules.name: scene_analysis_uses_grouping_principles
rules.head: the substrate processes multiple overlapping sound sources
rules.body: it groups by harmonic relations + common onset + common location + common modulation. Bregman 1990 ASA. Substrate's source-stream segregation.
